act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Punishment for Murder
original_text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_language: Applies when a person intentionally causes the death of another person or causes bodily harm knowing it is likely to cause death.
example_scenarios: A person intentionally attacks another with a deadly weapon with deliberate intent to cause death.
Acts committed with knowledge that death is the almost certain result.
punishment: Death or imprisonment for life, and fine.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Causing Death by Negligence
original_text: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
plain_language: Applies when a person causes death due to extreme carelessness, reckless driving, or failure to exercise reasonable caution without intention to kill.
example_scenarios: A driver over-speeds, passes a red light, and hits a pedestrian causing death.
A construction manager neglects basic safety gear causing a fatal accident.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Attempt to Murder
original_text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_language: Applies when someone takes an action attempting to kill another person, but the victim survives.
example_scenarios: Firing a gun at someone at close range, but the victim survives after medical intervention.
Stabbing a person in vital organs with intent to kill.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine; if hurt is caused, up to life imprisonment.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Voluntarily Causing Hurt
original_text: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 334, voluntarily causes hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
plain_language: Applies when someone intentionally causes physical pain, bodily harm, or illness to another person.
example_scenarios: Slapping or punching someone during a minor verbal argument.
Pushing someone causing minor bruises.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Voluntarily Causing Grievous Hurt
original_text: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 335, voluntarily causes grievous hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_language: Applies when someone causes severe bodily injury like fracture of bones, permanent loss of sight/hearing, disfigurement, or life-threatening harm.
example_scenarios: Attacking a person with a heavy rod breaking their arm or leg.
Striking someone's eye causing permanent blindness.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Wrongful Restraint
original_text: Whoever wrongfully restrains any person shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
plain_language: Applies when someone intentionally prevents another person from moving in a direction where they have a legal right to go.
example_scenarios: Blocking a hallway or doorway to physically prevent someone from exiting.
Stopping a vehicle on a public road to block someone's path.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹500, or both.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Assault or Criminal Force to Woman with Intent to Outrage Her Modesty
original_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_language: Applies when physical force or assault is used against a woman with the intention or knowledge of violating her modesty.
example_scenarios: Inappropriate physical contact or groping in a public or private setting.
Pulling a woman's clothing or physically grabbing her against her consent.
punishment: Imprisonment between 1 to 5 years, and fine.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Sexual Harassment
original_text: A man committing physical contact, unwelcome explicit sexual overtures, demanding sexual favours, or showing pornography against a woman's will shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment.
plain_language: Covers unwelcome physical contact, demands for sexual favors, showing pornography without consent, or making sexually colored remarks.
example_scenarios: Repeated unwelcome sexual remarks or demands made at workplace or educational institution.
Showing sexually explicit images/videos to someone without their consent.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Punishment for Rape
original_text: Whoever commits rape shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_language: Applies to non-consensual sexual acts under coercion, force, intoxication, deception, or absence of valid consent.
example_scenarios: Sexual assault committed without consent or under threat of physical harm.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment for at least 10 years up to life, and fine.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Theft
original_text: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, commits theft.
plain_language: Applies when someone dishonestly takes another person's movable property without their knowledge or consent.
example_scenarios: Stealing a laptop or wallet from an unattended desk or bag.
Taking a parked vehicle without permission.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Extortion
original_text: Whoever intentionally puts any person in fear of any injury to that person, or to any other, and thereby dishonestly induces the person so put in fear to deliver to any person any property or valuable security, commits extortion.
plain_language: Applies when someone blackmails or threatens harm to force a victim to surrender money, property, or documents.
example_scenarios: Threatening to release private photos unless money is paid.
Demanding protection money by threatening physical harm to a business.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Criminal Breach of Trust
original_text: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts that property to their own use commits criminal breach of trust.
plain_language: Applies when someone who was trusted with property or money dishonestly uses it for themselves instead of its agreed purpose.
example_scenarios: An employee or financial agent takes company funds for personal spending.
A bailee entrusted with jewellery sells it without authorization.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property
original_text: Whoever deceives any person and fraudulently or dishonestly induces that person to deliver property, or intentionally induces an act or omission causing harm, commits cheating.
plain_language: Covers deception that induces a victim to part with money, property, or consent based on false promises or fraudulent misrepresentation.
example_scenarios: An e-commerce seller takes payment online for goods while knowing they do not exist.
A fraudster promises guaranteed job placements in exchange for upfront cash.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Criminal Trespass
original_text: Whoever enters into or upon property in the possession of another with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy any person in possession of such property commits criminal trespass.
plain_language: Applies when someone unlawfully enters another person's house, land, or private premises to commit an offense, threaten, or harass them.
example_scenarios: Breaking into a private compound to intimidate the homeowner.
Encroaching physically into locked private property without legal right.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to ₹500, or both.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Forgery
original_text: Whoever makes any false document or false electronic record with intent to cause damage or injury, or to support any claim or title, commits forgery.
plain_language: Applies when someone creates fake signatures, altered contracts, counterfeit identity cards, or forged land records to deceive or defraud.
example_scenarios: Forging a landlord's signature on a property sale agreement.
Creating fake academic degree certificates to obtain employment.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Husband or Relative of Husband Subjecting Woman to Cruelty
original_text: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_language: Protects married women against physical or mental harassment, domestic abuse, or coercive dowry demands by husband or in-laws.
example_scenarios: Demanding additional cash/property from a bride's family accompanied by physical or emotional abuse.
Repeated domestic harassment causing danger to life, limb, or mental health.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Criminal Intimidation
original_text: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, with intent to cause alarm to that person, commits criminal intimidation.
plain_language: Applies when someone threatens death, severe injury, property destruction, or ruin of reputation to alarm or force a person to do something.
example_scenarios: Threatening a witness over phone to prevent them from testifying in court.
Sending threatening messages stating 'I will burn your house down'.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both; if threat is to cause death, up to 7 years.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
title: Word, Gesture or Act Intended to Insult the Modesty of a Woman
original_text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.
plain_language: Applies to catcalling, abusive language, obscene gestures, or invading a woman's privacy with intent to insult her modesty.
example_scenarios: Uttering vulgar remarks or making inappropriate obscene gestures at a woman in a public street.
Peeping into a private living area or invading personal privacy.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
source_reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860 / Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023

act_name: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
title: Application to Magistrate
original_text: An aggrieved person, Protection Officer, or any other person on behalf of the aggrieved person may present an application to the Magistrate seeking relief under this Act.
plain_language: A survivor of domestic violence, or someone acting for them, can ask a Magistrate for protection, residence, monetary, custody, or compensation orders.
example_scenarios: A woman seeks a protection order after threats or physical violence.
A survivor asks for residence and monetary relief.
jurisdiction_notes: Applications are usually made before the Magistrate with local jurisdiction.
source_reference: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

act_name: Right to Information Act, 2005
title: Request for obtaining information
original_text: A person who desires to obtain any information under this Act shall make a request in writing or through electronic means to the public authority.
plain_language: Any person can file an RTI request asking a public authority for information, with enough detail to identify the records requested.
example_scenarios: Requesting copies of municipal road work records.
Asking for status and file notes for a public service application.
jurisdiction_notes: The request should be sent to the correct public information officer.
source_reference: Right to Information Act, 2005

act_name: Information Technology Act, 2000
title: Punishment for Cheating by Personation by Using Computer Resource
original_text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
plain_language: Applies to online impersonation, phishing, fake social media profiles, or pretending to be a bank official online to steal money.
example_scenarios: Posing as a bank representative over WhatsApp/Email to steal OTPs and money.
Creating a fake executive profile to induce wire transfers.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to ₹1,00,000.
source_reference: Information Technology Act, 2000
